transcript:
Header: 2026-10-09 15:00 PDT | Duration: 42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Li (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Brooks (CrimsonPay HoP), Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng), Carlos Ruiz (SecOps), Samir Kaur (PM)

Summary: quick discovery to map integration points for CrimsonPay's payments QA assistant and routing features. Customer wants low-latency inference for fraud-detect and chat-style support; evaluating Hosted for speed-to-prod, Dedicated for predictable throughput, Private for data residency.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Maya our SE.
00:12 Evan: hey, hi, thanks, Evan here. We're excited to understand how Redwood fits our infra.
00:20 Maya: quick agenda, we'll ask about your stack and qps, then go over SDKs, integration options like LangChain / LlamaIndex, and then discuss rate limits, observability, and security. sound good?
00:32 Priya: yep, that's perfect. we want to see how invasive the integration is — ideally we call an SDK or via a gateway proxy.
00:44 Jordan: great. can you give a sense of traffic — qps, seq length, streaming needs?
00:52 Priya: baseline is say 50 qps for NLU scoring, peaks to 350 qps during batch reconciliation windows, average sequence len around 220 tokens, some streaming for agent chat with 300 token windows. those are rough.
01:12 Maya: good, that helps. for Hosted we have automatic autoscaling but quotas apply; for Dedicated you get reserved gpu pools and predictable throughput. Private gives you VPC/on-prem options with customer-controlled KMS.
01:30 Carlos: on security, SOC2 is required. we also need KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. can Redwood support HSM/KMS and SAML SSO?
01:44 Jordan: yes — SOC2 + ISO docs available, we integrate with KMS providers and can ship audit logs; SSO/SAML and RBAC supported. we'll include the security pack.
01:54 Priya: for the SDKs — do you provide first-class SDKs for Python/Node? And adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex?
02:05 Maya: yes. Python/Node SDKs, plus we maintain example adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex. we have a repo of notebooks that show how to wire Redwood streaming and function calls into LangChain chains and LlamaIndex indices. note: some of the adapter names in older docs show "RedwoodClient" which is a holdover, actual pkg name is redwood-sdk.
02:28 Samir: awesome. how about running through a quick example of how a request flows? especially in a gateway-proxy setup.
02:38 Maya: sure. Option A: Direct SDK call from service -> redwood-api (hosted) with token auth. Option B: you run an edge gateway/proxy in your VPC that forwards requests to Redwood; this is common when you want IP allow-listing or add local auth. Option C: for Private you run the control plane locally and connect to your internal infra. latency wise, direct hosted is lowest for general cloud usage; gateway adds ~10-30ms depending on placement.
03:05 Priya: and for rate-limiting, how do quotas behave? we need bursting up to concurrency of 400 qps occasionally.
03:14 Jordan: Hosted enforces quotas per account and per API key; default quotas are configurable and we can increase temporarily for POC. Dedicated gives you reserved throughput and predictable SLA; Private you size your cluster. Batching behavior can reduce token cost but might increase tail latency; we can tune batching windows.
03:34 Priya: is there a hard cap per second or a leaky-bucket style? we want to avoid 429s during reconciliation jobs.
03:42 Maya: it's token-aware leaky-bucket across routes, and we expose rate-limit headers. for large batch jobs we recommend using a separate route with higher quota or a bulk batch endpoint; we can also provide backpressure signals. we'll share sample quota configs.
03:58 Evan: observability is important — we need token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, traces that tie back to our request ids.
04:08 Maya: Redwood Console exposes per-route dashboards, token cost breakdowns, p50/p95/p99 latency and tracing hooks. we can instrument with OpenTelemetry or use our SDK hooks that emit traces and token counts. note: some of our older customers send events to Datadog and we have examples.
04:28 Carlos: can we get request/response logs without PII, and have them forwarded to our SIEM?
04:36 Jordan: yes, redaction options available; logs can be exported via syslog or S3 export into your pipeline. we'll include details in the security pack.
04:46 Priya: integration with LangChain — do you support streaming token callbacks into chains, and function/tool calling semantics?
04:56 Maya: yes streaming works with LangChain callbacks; our SDK exposes an async streaming API and a callback hook for tokens. function calling is supported — you can get structured JSON outputs. small caveat: sometimes LlamaIndex examples assume sync APIs; we'll include both sync and async patterns in the example notebooks.
05:18 Samir: what about embeddings and reranking? we plan an embeddings index at ~10M vectors.
05:27 Maya: embeddings are supported; for massive indexes we recommend a hybrid approach — store vectors in your vector DB (we integrate with common DBs) and use Redwood for embedding generation. cost and throughput depend on model and batch size; we'll provide guidance.
05:43 Priya: model selection — do you have curated models and quantization options? we want a balance of cost and safety.
05:52 Jordan: yes, model catalog with performance profiles. Redwood suggests quantized variants for Dedicated to reduce GPU memory and cost. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant/ batching for your workload.
06:06 Priya: about proxy auth — if we put a gateway in front, should it use API keys or mTLS towards Redwood?
06:14 Maya: both supported. gateway can present a single API key or we can mutually authenticate with mTLS for private deployments. Hosted supports API keys and token rotation.
06:26 Carlos: any known gotchas when proxying through a gateway? for example streaming chunking or timeouts?
06:33 Maya: yes streaming chunk size and timeout settings need to be tuned on the gateway. we also recommend sticky sessions for KV cache locality for chat use-cases; otherwise you can lose KV cache effectiveness. we'll share recommended Nginx/Envoy configs.
06:52 Evan: ok. pricing quick note — hosted is usage based per token, embeddings separate, dedicated is reserved GPU with monthly commit?
06:59 Jordan: correct. hosted per-token, dedicated reserved capacity (monthly/annual) plus overage, private is licensing + support. we'll send a pricing sheet.
07:10 Priya: for the POC, what's a minimal test we should run to validate latency and cost?
07:18 Maya: a small synthetic load: 5k requests at your avg seq len across 5 QPS with short bursts to 350, plus an embeddings batch. measure p95 latency, token cost, and success rate. we can also run a side-by-side against your current stack.
07:36 Samir: will you run any benchmarks or should we?
07:40 Maya: we can help run benchmarks in collaboration; for Dedicated we can provision a small reserved pool for the POC.
07:49 Priya: about contract and data residency — do you offer region pinning?
07:55 Jordan: yes, region pinning and private deployments for strict residency. we'll detail region availability in the docs.
08:03 Evan: ok, next steps recap please.
08:10 Jordan: sure. we'll send SOC2/security pack, example LangChain/LlamaIndex notebooks, SDK samples, recommended gateway configs, and pricing + dedicated options. Priya will send traffic profile. aim to kick off POC week of 10/20.
08:28 Priya: perfect, thanks.
08:32 Carlos: thank you. we'll review security docs and loop in GRC.
08:40 Jordan: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email with links.
